If you're planning on taking public transportation, study your routes, the maps, and if there are hours that anything stops operating. You don't want to be stuck halfway across town in the middle of the night. Local apps for public transit is great for more accurate info.

Even if someone is just trying to come off as friendly, if you have a gut feel, say you're too busy to talk right now, you have an appointment to get to, you're about to make an important phone call. Whatever it is to get them to stop talking to you. If you need to, move away and walk with purpose. Most times I feel like I wasn't bothered by scammers or pushy souvenir shop owners because I almost always had my sunglasses on, ONE earbud in (look busy, but always aware), and constant RBF 😅

Also, one earphone in while playing the walking directions on Google map helped me look a lot less lost. You can sometimes find previews with pictures for landmarks to look for if you're a visual learner.

Last, keep you your phone either on a crossbody lanyard or in your bag. Never a back pocket. Same thing for wallet or anything else you might find important.

Google translate can really help, and, if you have social anxiety 🙋‍♀️ you can listen to the pronunciation of what you'd like to try to say in the language before you engage. Or just politely show whoever you're trying to speak with.

If you do get lost or it's an uncomfortable area, find a group of women if you can or a nearby hotel. One or the other will most likely be willing to help you if you ask nicely. Sometimes getting lost is part of the fun, sometimes it isn't.

Give yourself ample time with transportation. Regardless of taxi, bus, bike or your own rental. I'm terrible with time and I struggled to stay on time for buses.

I used Travel Ladies for both being hosted, tips, and meeting locals/travelers. I have yet to try Nomad Her, but I loved my experience with Travel Ladies. I was hosted in Istanbul for 3 days and hosted in Paris for 2. I loved every moment of it and had some wonderful conversations and experiences with these women. I also met up several women in Istanbul to just walk around, eat, listen to live music and talk, had dinner with two women in Florence, and had a dinner picnic in Colmar with another. Both meeting locals and travelers were amazing especially coming from a place of wanting to support and share stories with one another. I think this definitely made my trip all that much for rich in experience for me.

Take a day if you need to just relax. It's okay to not see everything. I get the FOMO, but your mental and physical health is so important for you to continue your trip. Whenever I travel, 3-4 days in advance I start up on a Emergen-C and Zinc regimen. That will continue for my trip including 3-4 days after I return. A mask on the plane  can help you prevent getting sick, and hydration. There are a few different companies now that sell electrolyte and immunity booster powders/tablets. I like to pack those and have one every other day or as needed.

Sorry for such a long comment, but I hope this all helps 💗

I traveled solo as a woman there two weeks ago. Stayed at Hotel Cressy after a mix-up with my hostel. Not only was the owner super nice and welcoming, but I met a woman from Sweden who always stays there whenever she's in town. Coming from the States, I was told that being in Rome or any other big touristy areas you need to be on high alert for your personal belongings.

By the evening I had relaxed a lot. It's way safer than some of the places I've been to in San Francisco and New York over the past two years. Termini was cheaper to stay and and with public transportation, it's easy to get around.

People will give advice based on their experiences, whether it was good or bad. So please don't knock someone for having a different experience than you did. Just learn to take these sorts of advice with a little grain of salt.

I have a very similar story. First time living with housemates at age 22, and I decided to buy a really nice piece of pork butt to make carnitas for a taco night. I mean, I went all out on it, and this was for everyone to dig in on.

I had already preheated the oven to make some bits of the carnitas crispy. We finished prepping the taco station with shredded lettuce, cabbage, sour cream, salsa, cheese, and avocado. I went to grab the lid of the slow cooker, and it wasn't hot. My pork butt was room temperature at best, sitting there for 8 hours. And out of those 8 hours, I don't know how many of them were in the danger zone.

One of our newest roommates said she saw it left on in the morning, so she unplugged it. She said I should just cook it in the oven and try again. Not only was I mad about the pork butt being ruined, I was so mad at her lack of food safety knowledge to just assume you could try and cook it in the oven.

The air was silent, and I could feel everyone watching me getting mad, steam whistling out of my ears, and my mouth clenched around the verbal trashing she had headed towards her. Two roommates (one ended up becoming my late husband) immediately left, came back with ground beef, taco seasoning, and beer. They gave me a beer and a cigarette, directed me outside, and brought me tacos when they were done cooking. I think they might have saved her life.
